MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Health Care 

We are seeking an experienced Coding Auditor - Educator to support coding accuracy, data quality, and continuous improvement across our hospital network. This position is responsible for completion of coding audits for all SJG admissions to ensure accurate ICD-10-AM code assignment for data quality, benchmarking and funding. This position is also responsible for conducting and participating in audits based on health fund contracts, and the development of a contemporary coding audit framework.

Working closely with stakeholders across hospitals, you will identify short-, medium- and long-term training needs informed by audit outcomes, clinical documentation reviews, and feedback from clinical teams.

This is an excellent opportunity for a coding professional who is passionate about education, quality improvement, and influencing best practice within a values-driven healthcare organisation.

The Position

Conduct comprehensive audits of clinical coding to ensure accuracy and compliance with Australian Coding Standards and revenue integrity.

Assist with management of health fund contract audits.

Collaborate with SJGHC Coding Auditor-Educators in coordinating the audit and education cycle to identify areas for improvement and skill building with the objective of continually improving coding accuracy and optimising revenue.

Plan, develop and implement ongoing coding education for the National Coding Team ensuring programs enable the growth and development of both new and existing team members.

Assist with undertaking the coding trainee program.

Identify clinical documentation deficiencies during coding audit and provide documentation opportunity recommendations to the Clinical Documentation Specialists (CDS).

Maintain coding skills by regular completion of clinical coding.

You will bring a Bachelor of Health Information Management (or equivalent tertiary qualification) or a recognised Clinical Coding qualification. You will also demonstrate a minimum of five years' clinical coding experience, ideally gained within a tertiary hospital setting, supported by a strong understanding of coding standards and a commitment to accuracy and best practice.

You will bring strong verbal and written communication skills, along with solid PC proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office applications. About the Department - Program

Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.
